External / portable drive · Encrypted or locked

Recover Data From an Encrypted External Drive

Many external drives encrypt (scramble) their data, either with software such as BitLocker or Mac's built-in encryption, or with hardware encryption, as on many WD My Passport and My Book drives. Without the password or recovery key, recovery is not realistic.

3/5 · Take care
Success odds: Varies

Unlocking with a known key is low risk, but taking a hardware-encrypted drive out of its case can make the data unreadable.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Do not remove the drive from its case if it uses hardware encryption. The key may be tied to the bridge board, and a different adapter can show unreadable data.
  • Do not format or reset it. That destroys the key and the data.
  • Do not trust tools or people claiming to crack or brute-force strong encryption.

Your steps

0 of 6 done
  1. Show me how
    1. Look at the model name on the drive. WD My Passport and My Book often use hardware encryption, even if you never set a password.
    2. Windows: a padlock on the drive icon means BitLocker To Go. Mac: a password prompt when you plug it in means Mac encryption. VeraCrypt asks for a password in its own app.
  2. Show me how
    1. BitLocker: go to aka.ms/myrecoverykey (it opens account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey) on any device and sign in, or check a work or school account, a printed page or a saved file.
    2. Mac: use the password you set, which may be saved in Keychain Access (Applications, Utilities).
  3. Show me how
    1. For password-protected WD drives, download WD Security or WD Drive Utilities from the WD support site.
    2. Keep the drive in its original case, plug it in, open the software and type your password.
  4. Show me how
    1. Do not move the drive to another case or connect it directly to a computer.
    2. Keep the original USB cable and, if there is one, the power adapter.
  5. Show me how
    1. Copy your files to a different drive and open a few to check them.
    2. If the drive is also faulty, follow our imaging guide with ddrescue while it is unlocked and still in its case. Always type the failing drive first and the empty destination second. If you swap them, the copy erases your data.

    Guide: How to make an image (exact copy) of a drive

  6. Show me how
    1. If you have no password and no key, the data cannot realistically be recovered.
    2. If the drive is damaged and you do hold the key, ask a professional.

    Guide: How to find a trustworthy data recovery professional

Mission complete! 🎉 Check your recovered files open properly, then back them up in two places.

🧑‍🔧 When to call a pro

If the drive or its board is damaged and you hold the password or key, a professional may be able to help. Without the key, no one can realistically recover the data.

Questions people ask

Why is my WD drive unreadable outside its case?

Many WD My Passport and My Book drives encrypt data using a key tied to the bridge board (the small board that turns USB into the drive's own connection). A different adapter can leave the data unreadable.

Where is my BitLocker recovery key?

Often in your Microsoft account online, a work or school account, a printed page or a saved file.

Can someone crack it for me?

Not realistically. Strong encryption is designed to resist this, so be wary of anyone who says otherwise.

Before you start: Educational DIY guide, no warranty. DIY recovery can cause permanent data loss. If the data is valuable, consider a professional first.
